fatal_errors: The proposed supervised property-prediction model is not the target intervention of replacing liquid-phase EAM potentials with an MTP and replacing thermodynamic integration with free-energy perturbation.

The cited evidence concerns fabrication, mechanical properties, microstructure, or corrosion and provides no support for machine-learning prediction of melting thermodynamics, free energies, or computational acceleration.
The hypothesis omits the DFT/FEP mechanism, phase-space fidelity and energy-difference variance that enable rapid free-energy convergence.
No quantitative predictions are supplied for speedup, free-energy agreement, melting-point shifts, or model error.
The relevant validity conditions—TaVCrW, 0 GPa, GGA-PBE/LDA, high-temperature sampling, supercell size, and MTP training accuracy—are absent.
explanation: The response recognizes the broad objective of improving HEA melting predictions through machine learning, but it proposes a generic composition/processing/microstructure regression model rather than an atomistic machine-learning interatomic potential coupled to free-energy perturbation. Its baseline of CALPHAD also misses the relevant TOR-TILD/EAM and ab initio thermodynamic-integration baseline. The suggested train/test comparison using melting-temperature MAE and runtime is falsifiable in principle, but lacks a defined dataset, held-out compositional protocol, uncertainty treatment, and free-energy benchmark. Most importantly, none of the cited studies validates the intervention or even addresses melting-property prediction, so the central hypothesis is unsupported by the supplied evidence.
